original_metadata.title: A smooth connected manifold admits a locally homogeneous atlas modeled on some possibly disconnected Lie-group quotient exactly when a transitive Lie algebroid supports a flat geometrically closed Cartan connection
original_metadata.author: Anthony D. Blaom
original_metadata.source_title: The Infinitesimalization and Reconstruction of Locally Homogeneous Manifolds
original_metadata.difficulty_reason: The author constructs a global transitive Lie algebroid by gluing infinitesimal homogeneous actions, then reverses the construction through source-simply-connected integration and an equivariant developing map. The essential reverse direction controls isotropy closure, monodromy twists and chart transitions, and absorbs affine holonomy into a semidirect-product Lie group; these global integration and descent obligations go well beyond a local curvature calculation.

proof_review.note: Full two-way Theorem1.1 under the standing smooth connected-manifold hypothesis is selected. Read Section2 definitions, monodromy construction/Proposition2.6 and reverse quotient, all Section3 infinitesimal atlas gluing, all Section4 isotropy connectedness/development/equivariant-coordinate-change proof, and all Section5 reconstruction, including the semidirect-product conversion from affine transitions to genuine left translations. Geometric closure means the connected isotropy subgroup H0 in the simply connected integrating group G0 is closed, not just closed isotropy Lie algebra. Dazord integrability of action algebroids, Lie I/II and the prior local form of flat Cartan connections from [3] are published background, with exact author uses retained. The group G realizing the final atlas may be disconnected; no complete connection, global transitivity on M or universal-cover homogeneity is asserted. Theorem1.2 and completeness criteria are excluded from the count; all local constructions/supports are background within one packet.

original_metadata.statement_scope: Full Theorem1.1 with standing smooth connected M. Local homogeneity is an atlas whose transitions are restrictions of left translations on some homogeneous G/H, with G allowed to be disconnected. Equivalent condition: a transitive Lie algebroid g over M admits a linear Cartan connection (jet splitting a Lie algebroid morphism) that is flat and geometrically closed; the connected subgroup H0 with Lie algebra ker(anchor at m0), inside the simply connected group integrating the parallel-section Lie algebra, must be closed. Completeness is not assumed and global homogeneous-up-to-cover Theorem1.2 is not selected.
original_metadata.editorial_warning: Editorial note only: Proposition5.1 introduction writes the monodromy codomain as g0, while its item(2), Section2.6 and construction explicitly give Aut(g0). Lemma4.6/Proposition4.7 sometimes reverse the written tuple order (phi x mu) for the groupoid morphism previously defined in Lemma4.5 as (mu x phi); that defining derivative and the displayed commuting diagram identify the same authored morphism. All source pages are unchanged.
original_metadata.source_boundary_note: The full original two-way Theorem 1.1 is retained for a smooth connected manifold with complete author infinitesimalization, monodromy quotient, isotropy connectedness, development, equivariant coordinate changes and reconstruction. The new semidirect-product conversion from affine transition maps to genuine left translations is supplied. Geometric closure means the connected isotropy subgroup H0 is closed in the simply connected group G0, not merely a closed Lie subalgebra. Dazord integration, Lie I/II and the previously proved local form of a flat Cartan connection remain named published prerequisites with exact author uses. The realizing model group may be disconnected. Original monodromy-codomain and tuple-order notices are preserved. No completeness, universal-cover/global homogeneity or Theorem 1.2 assertion is selected.
